llm.summary: This Etsy category lookup skill should be reviewed because it also includes account login, API-key issuance, and billing/payment flows beyond simple lookup.

dimensions.detail: The scripts read LinkFox API keys and session/environment identifiers, make network requests, and allow endpoint base URLs to be overridden by environment variables. Network access is expected for LinkFox integration, but sending credentials to environment-selected hosts is under-scoped for sensitive authentication flows.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: I found no install-time hook or automatic execution path in the inspected artifact files. The risk comes from runtime instructions and optional scripts rather than installation behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger text activates on broad Etsy category/category-id requests, while onboarding instructions can steer users into phone-number, OTP, API-key, and payment workflows after auth or billing errors. Those sensitive flows are not scoped to explicit separate user intent at install-time.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The category script writes cached and full response data under a linkfox directory, the onboarding script writes QR image artifacts, and the onboarding guide recommends appending API keys to shell startup files. The login command also emits the API key in stdout JSON, which can be captured by logs or transcripts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Etsy category search, but the artifacts include SMS login, token exchange, API-key generation, plan listing, order creation, order querying, and payment QR rendering. Some onboarding is disclosed for auth and billing failures, but the capability set is high-impact and broader than a category lookup skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you expect this skill to manage LinkFox authentication and billing in addition to Etsy category lookup. Be prepared for it to handle a LinkFox API key, phone number, SMS code, account tokens, and payment-order data; review endpoint environment variables before use, avoid pasting secrets into shared logs, and manually confirm any plan or payment action.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: The artifact confirms environment-derived API bases are used for requests carrying API keys, session headers, phone/OTP login data, access tokens, refresh tokens, and generated API keys. This is not malicious by itself, but it is a real review concern because trusted destinations are not constrained in the artifact.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill is presented primarily as Etsy category lookup, but the inspected files require network access, credential handling, and file writes. Some of this is documented, but the authority is broader than a read-only lookup expectation.
[TP4] unexpected: The mismatch is materially supported: SKILL.md and references/onboarding.md route auth and billing errors into scripts/onboarding.py, which implements login, API-key retrieval, package purchase order creation, and QR payment generation.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The onboarding CLI’s documented subcommands and implementation confirm account onboarding, SMS login, API-key retrieval, plan purchase, and payment QR generation inside this category-search skill.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The authentication, API-key issuance, billing, order, and QR-code functions exist and are callable. They require user-provided phone/code or plan/method inputs, so I do not treat them as proven malicious, but they are high-impact and under-scoped for this skill.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The SKILL.md trigger is broad for Etsy category requests, and onboarding.md triggers on auth or billing errors. That can expose users to sensitive setup and payment flows from what begins as a lookup request.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The onboarding guide asks the agent to collect a phone number and SMS code and the login command returns an API key in stdout JSON. The artifact links agreements but does not add a clear agent-side consent, retention, or redaction policy.
[E1] expected: External transmission is expected for LinkFox API use, but the sensitive contents and environment-overridable destinations make this a review concern rather than a benign lookup-only data flow.
